After winning the 2002 NCAA Championship with [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], Blake was selected by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the 38th overall pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]]. Over his 13-year NBA career, Blake had stints with the Wizards, [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Denver Nuggets]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Detroit Pistons]], and three stints with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. ==High school career== Blake spent his freshman and sophomore year at [[Miami Killian High School]] and then transferred to [[Miami High School (Florida)|Miami High School]], where he played with another future NBA player, [[Udonis Haslem]]. Miami won consecutive state championships, but after the [[Miami New Times]] exposed the fact that Blake and other players, under head coach [[Frank Martin (basketball)|Frank Martin]] (himself later an NCAA Final Four coach), were using fake addresses to enroll in the school, the Stingarees were forced to forfeit their entire 1998 schedule.{{cite web |url=https://www.miaminewtimes.com/1998-03-05/news/dream-team/full/ |title=Dream Team|last=Powell |first=Robert Andrew |date=March 5, 1998|work=Miami New Times |access-date=April 4, 2009}}{{cite web |url=http://www.fhsaa.org/news/1998/0811.htm |title=Miami High School found guilty of FHSAA rules violations |last=Watford |first=Jack |publisher=[[FHSAA]] |date=August 11, 1998|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101125002247/http://fhsaa.org/news/1998/0811.htm|archive-date=November 25, 2010}}{{cite web|last=Powell|first=Robert Andrew|title=Disqualifying the Dream Team|url=https://www.miaminewtimes.com/1998-06-18/news/disqualifying-the-dream-team/full/|work=Miami New Time|access-date=February 21, 2014|date=June 18, 1998}} After the [[Florida High School Athletic Association|FHSAA]] banned him from playing for any public high school in Florida again, Blake attended [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] before enrolling at the University of Maryland. ==College career== After high school, Blake attended the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]]. Blake was the team's starter from the first game of his freshman year and was the first [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] player to compile 1,000 points, 800 assists, 400 rebounds and 200 steals. He finished his career 5th in NCAA all-time career assists with 972. Widely known for his superb passing ability, Blake helped lead the Terrapins to a [[Final Four]] appearance (2001) and the 2002 [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] championship; less well known for his scoring, Blake did average 11.6 points per game in his senior year.{{cite web|work=SportsStats |url=http://www.sportsstats.com/jazzyj/greats/03/blake.htm |title=Steve Blake, Maryland, 6–3, G |access-date=November 29, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080907165136/http://www.sportsstats.com/jazzyj/greats/03/blake.htm |archive-date=September 7, 2008 }} He averaged over six assists per game in each of his four years, including averages of 7.9 and 7.1 in 2002 and 2003, respectively. For his efforts, he was named to a variety of all-ACC teams during his career, including the rookie and defensive squads, capped by a first-team All-ACC spot his senior year. At the start of the 2003–04 basketball season, Blake's uniform number (25) became only the 15th to be retired to the rafters of Maryland's Comcast Center.{{cite web |url=http://umterps.cstv.com/ot/md-ask-testudo.html |title=Athletics – The University of Maryland Terrapins – Official Athletic Site |publisher=UMTerps.com |access-date=November 29, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216170101/http://umterps.cstv.com/ot/md-ask-testudo.html |archive-date=December 16, 2008 }} ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2003–2005)=== Blake was selected by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the 38th pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]]. He averaged 5.9 points, 2.8 assists, and 18.6 minutes per game while playing in 75 games his rookie season with the Wizards. In his second season Blake's playing time decreased to 14.7 minutes and only 44 games played. ===Portland Trail Blazers (2005–2006)=== [[Image:Steve Blake.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Blake with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]]] In September 2005, Blake (then a [[restricted free agent]] with the Wizards) was offered a contract by the Portland Trail Blazers, which the Wizards declined to match. This became the second reunion with former Maryland Terrapin and Washington Wizards backcourt teammate [[Juan Dixon]], who also signed with the Trail Blazers in the 2005 off-season. In Blake's first season with the Blazers, he became a starter and played a significant role when [[Sebastian Telfair]] was injured. Blake's playing time increased from 14.7 minutes and 44 games with only one start in [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05]] to 26.2 minutes and 68 games with 57 starts in [[2005–06 NBA season|05–06]]. Blake reestablished himself as a terrific passer and fundamental point guard claiming third in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] in assist-to-turnover ratio. He also increased his field goal percentage by 11%. ===Milwaukee Bucks (2006–2007)=== In July 2006, Blake was traded (along with [[Brian Skinner]] and [[Ha Seung-Jin]]) to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for [[Jamaal Magloire]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/Jamaal_Magliore-185803-1218.html |title=Trail Blazers Acquire All-Star Center Magloire |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 31, 2006}} ===Denver Nuggets (2007)=== On January 11, 2007, Blake was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in return for [[Earl Boykins]] and [[Julius Hodge]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2727760 |title=Nuggets deal Boykins, Hodge to Bucks for Steve Blake |last=Stein |first=Marc |work=[[ESPN]] |date=January 12, 2007}} Blake started in 40 of the 50 remaining games of the Nuggets' 2006–07 season, and in five playoff games in a 4–1 first-round loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. ===Second Portland Trail Blazers stint (2007–2010)=== Blake became an unrestricted free agent on July 1, 2007, and agreed to a three-year deal with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on July 13, 2007.{{cite news |url=http://www.rockymountainnews.com/drmn/nba/article/0,2777,DRMN_23922_5628146,00.html |title=Nuggets lose Blake |first=Aaron J. |last=Lopez |date=July 13, 2007 |work=[[Rocky Mountain News]] |access-date=July 13, 2007 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070715121821/http://www.rockymountainnews.com/drmn/nba/article/0,2777,DRMN_23922_5628146,00.html |archive-date = July 15, 2007}} The [[2008–09 Portland Trail Blazers season|2008–09 season]] saw a rise in Blake's numbers. Through his first 38 games, he averaged a career-high 11.7 points per game, while also achieving career highs in free throw percentage and three-point percentage.{{cite web |title=Steve Blake 2008–09 stats |publisher=NBA.com |access-date=January 21, 2009 |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/steve_blake/career_stats.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090130023631/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/steve_blake/career_stats.html |archive-date=January 30, 2009 }} On February 22, 2009, Blake tied an NBA record with 14 assists in the first quarter of a game against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web |url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5hapM0xex16cNEA_Kk_J4zidCxH6AD96GVVV80 |title=Blake, Trail Blazers top Clippers 116–87 |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=February 23, 2009}}{{dead link|date=June 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2010)=== On February 17, 2010, Blake was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with [[Travis Outlaw]] and $1.5 million in cash for [[Marcus Camby]].{{cite news|url=https://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2010/02/pritchard_trade_for_marcus_cam.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|title=Blazers-Clipper trade: Deal for Marcus Camby completed, Kevin Pritchard says|last=Quick|first=Jason|date=February 16, 2010}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2010–2014)=== [[Image:Steve Blake Lakers.jpg|thumb|230px|left|Blake being guarded by [[Nick Young (basketball player)|Nick Young]] of the [[Washington Wizards]]]] On July 8, 2010, Blake officially signed a four-year $16 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/100708lakerssignsteveblake.html |title=Lakers Sign Steve Blake |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=July 8, 2010}} In his first season for the Lakers, Blake averaged 4 points in 20 minutes per game. He missed games due to [[chicken pox]].{{cite news|last=McMenamin|first=Dave|title=Steve Blake finally settling in as a Laker|date=March 1, 2013|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/35940/steve-blake-finally-settling-in-as-a-laker|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130303165845/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/35940/steve-blake-finally-settling-in-as-a-laker|archive-date=March 3, 2013|url-status=live}} In his second season, he averaged 5.2 points in 23.2 minutes per game. He also played 5 of 53 games as a starter. He dealt with a [[costochondral]] fracture (fractured cartilage connecting the rib to the sternum). Statistically, he was a disappointment in those first two seasons under coach [[Phil Jackson]]'s [[triangle offense]] and then coach [[Mike Brown (basketball, born 1970)|Mike Brown]]'s [[post up|post-up]] offense, neither of which catered to his natural read-and-react skills. In the [[2012–13 Los Angeles Lakers season|2012–13 season]], his training camp was spoiled when he punctured his foot stepping on a spike strip in a beach parking lot. In November 2012, Blake was fined $25,000 by the NBA for inappropriate language towards a fan.{{cite news | url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/11/06/lakers-blake-fined/index.html | title=Lakers guard Blake fined $25,000 by league | work=NBA | access-date=November 6, 2012}} He started five straight games after a knee injury to starter [[Steve Nash]]. However, Blake was sidelined starting in November after suffering an abdominal strain that required surgery.{{cite news|title=Lakers top Kings, move to 2–0 since firing Mike Brown|date=November 11, Bazemore]].[http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/blaketrade_921914 Warriors Acquire Guard Steve Blake From Los Angeles Lakers] ===Third Portland Trail Blazers stint (2014–2015)=== On July 10, 2014, Blake web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/nets-acquire-rondae-hollis-jefferson-and-steve-blake|title=NETS ACQUIRE RONDAE HOLLIS-JEFFERSON AND STEVE BLAKE|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, 2015|access-date=July 14, 2015}} Blake's final NBA game was played in Game 4 of the 2016 Eastern Conference First Round on April 26, 2016. The Pistons would lose the game 98–100 to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with Blake recording 3 points, 2 assists and 1 rebound. ===Sydney Kings (2016)=== On October 22, 2016, Blake signed with the [[Sydney Kings]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 NBL season]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sydneykings.com/featured-news/kings-add-experienced-nba-guard/|title=KINGS ADD EXPERIENCED NBA 5.9 points, 2.3 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game. ==Coaching career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2017–2019)=== On September 27, 2017, Blake was reported to have joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as a coaching intern.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/northwest/portland-trail-blazers/breakfast-blazers-steve-blake-returns-time-coach|title=Breakfast with the Blazers: Steve Blake returns, this time as coach|date=September 27, 2017|work=nbcsports.com|access-date=September 27, 2017}} For the [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]], Blake was promoted to an on-court assistant for the Trail Blazers.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/06/26/suns-complete-coaching-staff-official-release|title=Phoenix Suns announce complete coaching staff}} ===Phoenix Suns (2019–2020)=== On June 26, 2019, Blake was hired as an assistant coach for the Phoenix Suns.
